'''''Erodium botrys''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Geraniaceae|geranium family]] known by the common names '''longbeak stork's bill''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=ERBO|taxon=Erodium botrys|accessdate=19 January 2016}}</ref> '''Mediterranean stork's-bill'''<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> and '''broadleaf filaree'''.

==Distribution==
This is an annual herb which is native to much of [[Eurasia]], the [[Mediterranean region]], and [[North Africa]].

It is found in many other areas of the world as a weedy  [[introduced species]], including Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, and parts of the Americas.

==Description==
''Erodium botrys'' starts from a flat rosette of highly lobed green leaves on red [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]]. It grows to heights of anywhere from {{convert|10|to|90|cm|sp=us}} with somewhat hairy stems and foliage.

It bears small flowers with hairy, pointed [[sepal]]s surrounding five purple-streaked lavender petals.

The [[Erodium|filaree]] fruit is quite long, its style reaching up to {{convert|12|cm|sp=us}} in length.
